title: The Lost Child
text: A child sits on a stone by the road, crying quietly into her sleeve, dressed in a smock and bonnet for a town that burned a hundred years ago. There is soot on her cheeks. She does not seem to have grown up at all, and she does not seem to know.

options.label: Take the child along. No one should be left alone out here.

outcomes.text: The child walks with you as far as the next bend, smiles, and is gone. The air smells of bread, and of smoke.
The child is not a child, and it has been waiting for someone kind.

options.label: The sharpest asks her questions first, gently, before anyone takes her hand.

outcomes.text: Its answers are wrong in small ways, and the questions tell you a great deal about what lives here.

options.label: Leave her on her stone. Whatever she is, she has waited a hundred years already.

outcomes.text: The crying follows you for hours, and then it stops, which is worse.
